candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safe medication administration, adverse effects, interactions and teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret serum digoxin monitoring correctly by recognizing appropriate sampling time and the need to correlate a level with the client's clinical status.

options.A: Treat the result as a steady-state trough because serum digoxin concentrations are interpreted the same regardless of when the sample is drawn.
options.B: Increase the next dose if the result is lower than expected because an early post-dose level reliably represents the tissue concentration at the end of the dosing interval.
options.C: Stop all future digoxin doses solely from this one sample because any post-dose concentration is sufficient to diagnose toxicity without clinical correlation.
options.D: Interpret the result cautiously and obtain a properly timed level—just before the next dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose—while considering the clinical picture.

candidate.rationale: Digoxin labeling directs clinicians to interpret serum concentrations in the overall clinical context and not use an isolated value alone for dose changes. A serum digoxin concentration should be obtained just before the next scheduled dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose; a sample drawn 2 hours after dosing is too early for routine therapeutic interpretation.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Serum digoxin concentrations should be interpreted in clinical context and sampled just before the next scheduled dose or at least 6 hours after the last dose.
candidate.source_locator: Digoxin label §2.5, Monitoring to Assess Safety, Efficacy, and Therapeutic Blood Levels — interpret in clinical context; obtain just before next dose or ≥6 hours after last dose
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine; FDA-approved labeling)
candidate.stem: A client taking once-daily digoxin has a serum digoxin concentration drawn 2 hours after the morning dose. The client has no new symptoms. Which nursing interpretation is most appropriate?
